priceSnapshot.note: THIS IS THE REAL END-DAY RUN, at 19:37 COT on the correct clock. It overwrites a file that already carried the id 2026-08-21-endday: that earlier file was written at 08:40 COT by a mislabelled catch-up run and priced BTC at 76,919.9. Its calibration row is left untouched in the history, but everything below is fresh. WHAT HAPPENED SINCE MIDDAY: the midday report at 12:45 COT framed a 76,222.2 to 78,258.6 range with spot at 77,410.8 and put 18 USDT of idle cash into the spot core. The range top BROKE. Settled 1H closes of 78,458.2, 78,511.5 and 78,339.3 all cleared 78,258.6, so the midday add gate fired by up to 252.9 points, and price ran to 78,759.2 at 23:15Z. It has since given back 787.0 points, a 1.00 percent fade, and the last thirty-five minutes contained the first genuine long-liquidation cascade of the entire advance - 2.25 million USD of forced selling on the OKX perp between 00:04Z and 00:21Z, of which 99.99 percent was longs. Spot is 77,972.2, up 561.4 points on the midday mark and up 5.78 percent on twenty-four hours. The session since the midday snapshot has traded 76,621.4 to 78,759.2, a 2,137.8 point band against a 1H ATR of 880.3. Note that 78,759.2 is a LOWER high than yesterday's 79,515.7 spike, so the day did not make a new extreme.

This replaces the 76,222.2 line the midday run used, because the market has since spent nine hours building structure above it and the honest break point has moved up with the tape. Give it room on purpose: spot is 1,350.8 points above it, which is 1.53 hourly ATRs, so an ordinary hour can reach it without meaning anything - the trigger is a settled CLOSE, not a touch. Below it the CoinGlass 48-hour Model 3 map offers a 467.02K band at 76,462.6 and then thins out badly until the 874.85K band at 74,327.0.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $78,759.2 - the high of the 23:15Z bar and the top of this session. The old 78,258.6 gate has already fired and is now support-in-waiting, so the next real signal has to be a close above the session high. Reclaiming it would put the 78,935.4 CoinGlass band and then yesterday's 79,515.7 spike high back in play. The caveat is the same one the midday report raised and it has if anything strengthened: above spot the 48-hour heatmap shows one 404.90K band at 78,935.4 and essentially nothing else before 80,000, so a break up walks into unmapped air and has to be paid for with real spot demand rather than forced short covering. On the fresh OKX tape the short liquidations that would fuel such a squeeze totalled 289 USD against 2,252,965 USD of long liquidations.

decisionBox.changed: The stance moves from ADD to TAKE_PROFIT, and this is a trim rather than an exit. Three things changed in the nine hours since midday and all three point the same way. First, the range top broke and the move immediately failed to hold: 78,759.2 was rejected and 787.0 points have come back out, with the day printing a LOWER high than yesterday's 79,515.7. Second, the derivative tape finally cracked - 2.25 million USD of forced liquidations on the OKX perp inside seventeen minutes, 99.99 percent of it longs, clustered at 77,826.6, 77,965.1 and 78,090.1, which is exactly the band price just fell through. Venue open interest reads 2,319,564,209 USD against 2,331,486,229 at midday, down 0.51 percent, so this leg was NOT accompanied by fresh money the way the earlier ones were; positions closed instead. Third, the oscillators are where they have been all week and it still matters: 4H RSI 89.75 and daily RSI 86.17, spot 15.63 percent above the daily EMA20 at 67,435.1 and 9.62 percent above the daily EMA200 at 71,132.2. Against that, the trend case is genuinely intact - price is above all four EMAs on all four timeframes, and Farside now shows a FIFTH straight ETF inflow day. So the wallet trims 20 percent of the spot core at 77,972.2, roughly 0.00031361 BTC for about 24.45 USDT, and keeps the other 80 percent. The reason the size is small is the honest one: this file's own record shows the 20 August morning trim at 71,892.5 was punished, and selling strength in a confirmed-inflow uptrend has been the recurring error here. The reason the trim happens at all is the seventeen-hour gap - the next report is ~02:00 tomorrow, and the entire mapped liquidity on the 48-hour heatmap sits BELOW: 467.02K at 76,462.6, 874.85K at 74,327.0 and 1.22M at 72,191.4, which is the brightest band on the whole chart and 7.41 percent under spot. A resting stop at 76,600.0 is recommended for the same reason.

overnightRisk: The next report is ~02:00 tomorrow, roughly six and a half hours away, but the gap that actually matters is the weekend one that starts now: it is Friday 19:37 COT, the US cash session has closed, QQQ finished at 713.44 and VOO at 703.71, and the 10-year settled at 4.736 percent up 0.038 on the day. Crypto trades through and everything else does not, so from here until Monday BTC absorbs any headline alone and on thin books. Three specific hazards. FIRST, the liquidity is one-sided and it is all beneath: the CoinGlass 48-hour Model 3 map shows 467.02K at 76,462.6, 874.85K at 74,327.0 and a 1.22M band at 72,191.4 - the brightest on the entire chart, 5,780.8 points and 7.41 percent below spot - against a single 404.90K band at 78,935.4 above and nothing meaningful before 80,000. A flush has somewhere to be pulled to and a rally does not. SECOND, the flush has already started in miniature: 2,252,965 USD of long liquidations against 289 USD of short liquidations on the OKX perp between 00:04Z and 00:21Z, with the heaviest single fill 8.9989 BTC at 77,826.6. That is 145 points under spot as this is written, so the market is currently sitting directly on top of the level where the last cascade cleared. THIRD, open interest is no longer confirming: 2,319,564,209 USD on the OKX venue against 2,331,486,229 at midday, down 0.51 percent while price rose - the first time in this advance that a new high has come without new money behind it. The offsetting catalyst is real and should be named: Farside's 21 August row prints +68.2 million USD with IBIT still showing a dash, meaning the largest fund has not reported and the true number is very likely higher. That would make five consecutive inflow days totalling at least 1,678.5 million USD, and it is the single strongest argument that this is spot-led rather than leverage-led. The concrete plan is therefore a resting stop rather than a forecast: 76,600.0, just under the 76,621.4 session low, accepting that a fill there can slip into the 76,462.6 band 137 points lower. Above, a settled 1H close over 78,759.2 reopens the upside. Between the two, nothing needs doing.

calibration.note: The midday report named the range at 76,222.2 to 78,258.6 and the upper gate fired. Settled 1H closes of 78,458.2, 78,511.5 and 78,339.3 all cleared 78,258.6, the best of them by 252.9 points, so add_fired is true. The reduce line at 76,222.2 was never threatened - the lowest point of the whole session was 76,621.4, some 399.2 points above it, and the lowest settled 1H close was 77,024.9 - so reduce_fired is false. The action stands up too: midday deployed 18.00 USDT into the spot core at 77,410.8 and spot is 77,972.2, worth about 0.13 USDT more, or +0.73 percent. Small, but the right sign, and it reverses the pattern of the 20 August morning run that trimmed into strength and lost 0.45 USDT for it. The morning row of 21 August is also being closed out here: it named 76,422.3 and 78,258.6, neither fired before the midday report, and its price_next_report is 77,410.8. One honest caveat on the record itself - a mislabelled 08:40 COT catch-up run already wrote a row for date 2026-08-21 session endday. That row is left in place; this run appends its own.
